blind_spots.blind_spot: The product is sold as cloud AI-SaaS while the customers named in their own SBIR abstracts — SDA, JADC2, ABMS — operate on classified fabric where that delivery model is the gate, not the feature
blind_spots.operator_reality: An SDA or ABMS mission thread runs on SIPR or higher. Getting CNTIENT there means an ATO on a network where the model cannot phone home, cannot pull telemetry from a commercial cloud, and cannot be retrained on live data. The 87%-per-operator saving was measured on the commercial side of that boundary; on the classified side the same software is a different program with a different accreditation owner and an 18-month clock. 'Request Access/Demo' is not a path a program office can follow.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their commercial constellation business (Terran Orbital and similar operators) works exactly as advertised over the open internet, so cloud delivery has never cost them a deal. The classified variant only becomes the whole project after the demonstration ends, which is precisely when the funded months run out.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: By leveraging artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and deep operational expertise, Cognitive Space provides automated satellite operations that enable constellations to scale

blind_spots.blind_spot: A reinforcement-learning scheduler that beats a greedy heuristic by 4x has no stated explainability, repeatability, or manual-fallback story — and that is what an accrediting authority and an ops crew will ask for first
blind_spots.operator_reality: A space operations crew commander cannot execute a collection or link-management plan they cannot explain to the mission director, and cannot accept a planner that produces a different answer on the same inputs. The question at the operational acceptance review is not 'how much better is it' but 'what does the crew do at 0300 when the plan looks wrong, and how do they revert.' Nothing in their language names a fallback mode, a determinism guarantee, or a human-approval step. A 4x benchmark does not survive that meeting.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Both open engineering roles are reinforcement-learning positions, so the internal scoreboard is model performance against a baseline. Trust engineering — the deterministic replay, the audit trail, the degraded manual mode — is nobody's job title in a 24-person company.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Dynamically reschedule mission plans in near real-time

blind_spots.blind_spot: Their own problem statement names downlink as the bottleneck, yet the architecture is a ground-based planner whose value depends on the very ground segment and links it cannot control
blind_spots.operator_reality: If the constraint is 'Bottlenecks in data downlink' and 'Near real-time response requirements', then plan quality is capped by how fast a new plan reaches the vehicle. In a contested or degraded ground-station picture — the AFRL quote is explicitly about the oversubscribed AF Satellite Control Network — a planner sitting in a cloud produces optimal plans that arrive after the pass. The frame-rate lesson applies directly: the answer is decoupling planning from the uplink cadence and pushing autonomy on board, not making the ground-side optimizer smarter.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: They correctly diagnosed the bottleneck on their own homepage and then built the solution on the side of it that is easiest to sell as SaaS. Commercial operators with plentiful commercial ground networks never expose the failure; a contested tactical ISR timeline does.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Increasing complexity in payloads and taskability / Fast-growing constellations / Oversubscribed capacity / Near real-time response requirements / Bottlenecks in data downlink

opener_hook: Your homepage lists 'bottlenecks in data downlink' as the problem and then quotes AFRL on the oversubscribed AF Satellite Control Network — which means CNTIENT's 87% operator saving is being measured on the side of the link that isn't the constraint.
what_they_do: AI software (CNTIENT) that automates mission planning, tasking, and ground-pass scheduling across satellite constellations, sold to commercial imagery operators and to SDA/AFRL for ISR collection and mesh-network link management.
